title: Vigil held for immigrant community following ICE raid in Elgin - NewsBreak
text:
By Jenna Barnes Ethan Illers ,
1 hours ago
ELGIN, Ill. ( WGN ) – Faither leaders, elected officials and community organizers came together at Elgin’s First Presbyterian Church Wednesday evening to pray for and support Elgin’s immigrant community.
The vigil was organized by the group Centro de Informacion in the wake of Tuesday’s early-morning ICE raid. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem joined ICE on the ground in Elgin during the raid and posted videos of the immigration enforcement.
WGN-TV has since learned two of the people arrested were U.S. citizens and have been released.
ICE agents target roofers in Naperville, leaving workers and residents shaken “[Noem] shows up when it’s convenient for social media purposes to drive a narrative,” Dianha Ortega-Ehreth of Centro de Informacion said.
“Using the military style tactics that they used in a quiet community just shows that they’re not really interested in public safety,” State Rep. Anna Moeller (43rd District) added.
More ICE activity was spotted in the northwest and western suburbs on Wednesday.
Community rapid response teams documented an encounter in Wheaton, where they questioned the ICE team and demanded to see a judicial warrant.
The agents left without making an arrest.
SEE ALSO: DHS Secretary Kristi Noem visits Chicago area Tuesday, dozens arrested since start of ‘Operation Midway Blitz’ ICE agents also continue to stake out local jails, looking to detain people as they’re released from custody.
Video obtained by WGN Investigates shows agents in the public lobby of the Kane County Jail in St. Charles, taking a man into custody on Wednesday as well. It’s unclear why the man had been in jail or why ICE targeted him.
“We have to get out there every single morning, even though we’re scared,” Ortega-Ehreth said.
Despite the increased attention, the work doesn’t stop or organizations providing social services to immigrant communities.
VIDEO: Here’s how ICE agents operate at courthouses, inside jails At the Elgin vigil, Maggie Lugo, executive director of Casa Michacan, explained she came to the U.S. as a child and is undocumented.
“I walk in fear, but I also know that I know my rights. I know that I pay my taxes, I know that I have two U.S. citizen kids that were born here, that are educated to stand up for their communities,” Lugo said. “I love America.”
